title: Forming shared attention between robot and users in conversational situations

fields.value: Technical system description with experimental evaluation.

quotes.text: This paper proposes an algorithm that enables shared attention between a robot and speakers in alternative conversational situations.

In order to show the effectiveness of the method for alternatively forming shared attention with speakers in a conversational scene involving multiple users, we conducted an experiment as shown in Fig. 9.

fields.value: The authors report that integrating skin-color information with audio/depth-based sound localization reduced errors: localization error was within 0.1 m for all 87 voiced frames, versus within 0.15 m for 94.3% of frames using audio alone. The speaker and attention target were reported as correctly detected in the alternating-conversation demonstration. No statistical significance test is stated.

fields.value: The paper frames the behaviour as forming shared attention between a robot and users in conversation. It specifically targets overt attention, where the user's attention target matches the object being fixated on.

quotes.text: In this paper, we define as “shared attention” the robot identifying the object (an object or a person) that the user is attending to and sharing it as an object of attention.
This paper targets “overt attention,” which can be handled objectively based on image information.

fields.value: Shared attention is defined as the robot identifying what a user attends to and sharing that object as an attention target. The paper treats overt attention as the case where the attention target and fixation target coincide.

quotes.text: In this paper, we define as “shared attention” the robot identifying the object (an object or a person) that the user is attending to and sharing it as an object of attention.
“Overt attention” is the case in which the attention target coincides with the fixation target.

fields.value: The robot detects and selects the current speaker, identifies the speaker's attention target, and shares it to support communication in turn-taking conversation.

quotes.text: In order to realize shared attention with multiple users in a conversational scene, it is necessary to: 1) detect and select the speaker to whom the robot should attend; 2) detect the gaze direction, face direction, and pointing direction of the attended speaker; 3) extract the speaker's attention target from the image; and 4) direct the robot's attention to the extracted target.

Furthermore, a method for identifying the speaker's attention target using a saliency map calculated based on estimation of the speaker's three-dimensional head posture was applied in coordination with speaker changes.

fields.value: The system demonstrated alternating shared attention with speakers and detected their attention targets. The paper does not report measured effects on users or interaction outcomes beyond system performance.

fields.value: An autonomous algorithm fuses a five-channel microphone array, three-eye stereo camera texture/depth images, and skin-color likelihood maps to locate the speaker. It detects the face, estimates 3D head pose using a wireframe model, propagates visual-acuity values over time to create a saliency map, extracts the attention target using CamShift, and displays the target image to the speaker.

quotes.text: The robot's head is equipped with a three-eye camera capable of stereo vision, and can measure the depth distance of the environment.
A five-channel microphone array is implemented at the front of the robot body.
The skin-color likelihood map and the sound source localization likelihood map are linearly combined according to equation (9).
The saliency map of shared attention is calculated by adding the visual-acuity maps over time with a temporal decay weight.

fields.value: An omnidirectional mobile robot with a three-eye stereo camera on its head and a five-channel microphone array at the front of its body.

fields.value: The paper presents and tests a robot system that follows alternating conversation between two users, identifies the current speaker and estimates what that speaker is attending to. In its demonstration, the system detected attention targets as speakers changed; combining audio localization with image-based skin-color information also improved reported speaker-location accuracy.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper defines shared attention and overt attention, describes the behaviour's role in alternating conversation, details its sensing and processing implementation, and specifies the robot platform. It does not establish effects on people or discuss how embodiment influenced the study.
